labxchange_results.title: Organic Chemistry
labxchange_results.description: Organic chemistry is the study of the molecules that are necessary for life to exist. The key ingredient for these molecules is carbon, which is able to form complex structures and allows for the variety of different molecules in living things. This pathway provides resources for understanding the basic rules that are used to categorize these different molecules.
learning_objectives: Identify the homologous series that a n organic molecule belongs to.
Name an organic molecule based on the iupac rules.
Diagram an organic molecule based on its iupac name.
Recall the functional groups of the various homolgous series.

labxchange_results.title: When Chemicals Meet Water: The Properties of Solutions
labxchange_results.description: This unit addresses the physical and chemical properties of solutions. Although several topics addressed are common to all solution-phase systems, most of the examples are based specifically on aqueous systems since these are fundamental to life and common in inorganic chemistry. This unit forms part of Chemistry: Challenges and Solutions.
learning_objectives: Identify the solvent and solute(s) in different types of solutions.
Describe differences in solubility behaviors for solid, liquid, and gas solutes.
Calculate concentrations of solutions and understand the differences between different concentration units.
Discuss how solutions’ physical properties differ from those of pure solvents, and how concentration affects the extent of these differences.

labxchange_results.title: The Surprising Organic Chemistry
labxchange_results.description: One of the most important and interesting areas in science is organic chemistry. This is the study of carbon and its compounds. Organic chemistry is a big part of our everyday life because it covers more than 90% of all known substances, both natural and man-made. It also connects closely with many other fields of science. In this pathway, we will explore the basics of organic chemistry, including its origins, the compounds it studies, their properties, and their uses. Let's dive into the fascinating world of organic chemistry!
learning_objectives: Assess the importance of organic chemistry, from the description of its implications in technological, economic, ecological development and the discussion of the relationships it maintains with other sciences such as inorganic chemistry, medicine, biochemistry.

Describe the importance of functional groups in determining the physical-chemical properties of organic compounds, from their identification in open formulas, the interpretation of the concept of isomerism, the molecular representation and the application of the IUPAC system for their nomination.
Classify chemical functions from the recognition of their nomenclature, their particular properties and the observation and identification of said properties in laboratory experiences.

Recognize the importance of hydrocarbons in the industry, from the description of their properties, classes, methods of obtaining, forms of representation and nomenclature; and the observation, identification and interpretation of their characteristics in experimental processes in which they will work with alkanes, alkenes and alkynes.

labxchange_results.title: Proteins
labxchange_results.description: This pathway explores the structure and folding of proteins. Proteins are large biomolecules, or macromolecules, consisting of one or more long chains of amino acid residues. Proteins perform a vast array of functions within organisms, including catalyzing metabolic reactions, DNA replication, responding to stimuli, providing structure to cells and organisms, and transporting molecules from one location to another. Proteins differ from one another primarily in their sequence of amino acids, which is dictated by the nucleotide sequence of their genes, and which usually results in protein folding into a specific three-dimensional structure that determines its activity.
learning_objectives: Describe the four levels of protein structure.
Explain the thermodynamic factors that influence protein folding.
Discuss the kinetics of protein folding.

game_1782308849318_rdrc.html:
官能团改造沙盒台
M04 / RDKit LAB

项目路线

本关目标

给骨架挂官能团, 把溶解度条推过达标线 —— 造出一个能溶于水的分子怪兽。

官能团调色板 (拖到挂点)

操作说明

1 从调色板把官能团拖到分子上的灰色挂点。2 或直接拨滑块批量挂 -OH。3 看右侧溶解度条变化。4 推过虚线即达标。

分子怪兽改造台
目标: 溶解度 > 60
疏水指数 logP 2.1
溶解度 18
项目终点: 分子怪兽图鉴
这一步 = 学会用官能团调性质
真实化学: -OH/-NH2/-COOH 能跟水形成氢键 → 更亲水更易溶; -CH3/苯环是疏水基 → 拉低溶解度。挂越多亲水基, 条越长。

exercises.question: 什么是「官能团」？
options: 分子骨架里那一长串连起来的碳
挂在分子骨架上、决定分子脾气（性质）的一小撮抱团出现的原子
分子的总重量
把分子写成字符的一种写法
exercises.explanation: 官能团就是挂在分子身子（骨架）上的「小零件 / 工具」——像钥匙、像小水桶，个头不大，却专门决定这个分子的脾气（爱不爱溶水、活不活泼）。-OH 和 -NH2 都是官能团。
exercises.ref: 用老师给的 RDKit 代码模板, 对同一个骨架算出加官能团之前/之后的性质(如亲水性/LogP), 整理成一份官能团改造对照记录(上电脑需家长协助, 用现成代码模板只改要读的分子)

exercises.question: 给一个分子加上 -OH 这个官能团，通常会让它怎么样？
options: 变得更躲水、更不溶于水
变得更亲水、更容易溶于水
重量变成原来的两倍
颜色一定会变红
exercises.explanation: -OH（一个氧加一个氢）是个亲水的小零件，挂上去会让分子更爱跟水待在一起。乙烷几乎不溶于水，只加一个 -OH 变成乙醇后，就能和水痛快地混在一起了。
exercises.ref: 用老师给的 RDKit 代码模板, 对同一个骨架算出加官能团之前/之后的性质(如亲水性/LogP), 整理成一份官能团改造对照记录(上电脑需家长协助, 用现成代码模板只改要读的分子)

exercises.question: 做「对照实验」时，最关键的一条规矩是什么？
options: 一次把能改的地方全改了，变化才明显
每次只改一个地方，别的全都不动
实验做得越快越好
改动越多，越能看清是谁的功劳
exercises.explanation: 对照实验的看家法宝就一条：每次只改一个地方，别的按兵不动。这样性质一旦变了，就只能赖在这唯一改动的那一处头上——就像查「多浇水是不是让花更高」，得两盆花别的全一样，只让一盆多浇水。
exercises.ref: 用老师给的 RDKit 代码模板, 对同一个骨架算出加官能团之前/之后的性质(如亲水性/LogP), 整理成一份官能团改造对照记录(上电脑需家长协助, 用现成代码模板只改要读的分子)

exercises.question: 把乙烷（一段光秃秃的短碳链）只加一个 -OH 变成乙醇，它从「几乎不溶于水」变成了「能溶于水」。这件事说明了什么？
options: 分子的性质跟结构没关系
结构决定性质——结构上改一点点，性质就能跟着大变
只有加很多个官能团才会改变性质
乙烷和乙醇其实是同一个分子
exercises.explanation: 这正是化学里最重要的铁律「结构决定性质」：骨架没变，只多挂了一个 -OH，溶不溶水这件大事就整个翻了过来。结构动一丁点，性质就能天翻地覆——这是后面工作台「看结构、推性质」的根本前提。
exercises.ref: 用老师给的 RDKit 代码模板, 对同一个骨架算出加官能团之前/之后的性质(如亲水性/LogP), 整理成一份官能团改造对照记录(上电脑需家长协助, 用现成代码模板只改要读的分子)

exercises.question: 这一节你要亲手交出的成果（产物）是什么？
options: 一张用纸笔画的官能团概念图
一份用 RDKit 算出加 -OH 前 / 后性质（如 LogP）并排对照的「官能团改造对照记录」
背下「结构决定性质」这句话
把整本化学书抄一遍
exercises.explanation: 这是真实动作节点：你要用 RDKit 对同一个骨架，算出加 -OH 之前和之后的性质数字（亲水性 / LogP），把这一前一后并排记下来，亲眼用工具量出「改结构 → 性质变」的因果。产物是这份真实的对照记录，不是「懂了」而已。
